clue.text: Loopy joiner, general pain

parts.note: blanket as an adjective means general or covering everything, as in a blanket ban
a stitch is a sharp pain in the side

explanation.surface: A crazy carpenter is a general nuisance to everyone around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loopy joiner' reads as a mad woodworker, but it describes a sewing stitch worked in loops that joins or edges fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: This embroidery stitch forms a row of loops along an edge, joining or finishing cloth, so it is a looped joining stitch.

clue.text: Nothing alongside feature is material

parts.note: the chin is one of the features of the face
nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Having nothing apart from a single feature is the stuff of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alongside' simply places the two pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Chino is a twilled cotton fabric, the cloth used for chinos trousers.

clue.text: Elected official might, amongst gracious men

indicators.note: amongst means the word for might sits in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: Gracious! and Lord! are both exclamations of surprise
OR, other ranks, is the usual crossword abbreviation for ordinary soldiers or men
may is an old noun for might or power, as in might and main

explanation.surface: An elected official may wield might amongst courteous gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gracious' is not an adjective about the men but an exclamation, like 'Good Lord!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a city corporation in Britain is chosen by election from the council, so it is an elected civic office.

clue.text: Long canine having trouble with meat

parts.note: a sausage is a type of meat product
to dog someone is to trouble or plague them

explanation.surface: A tall dog is having digestive trouble after eating meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dachshund is nicknamed this informally because of its very elongated body, so it is a long dog.

clue.text: Flag of West European? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short of completion and loses its last letter

parts.note: the Irish are a people of western Europe

explanation.surface: Asking whether some national flag belongs to a western European country, but not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a national banner, but it is the yellow flag, a wild flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a common name for certain wild irises, such as the yellow water plant growing by ponds.

clue.text: Report the core of each matter

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letters, here the inner pair of the word each

parts.note: to count means to matter, as in every vote counts

explanation.surface: A report gets to the heart of each issue.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a narrative or report of events, as in giving an account of what happened.

clue.text: Opposite directions taken in characteristic route

indicators.note: taken in means the compass points are absorbed into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing characteristic
north and south are opposite compass directions, N and S

explanation.surface: A path taken in opposite directions has its own distinctive way.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit means passage or the way taken from one place to another, as in a route for goods.

clue.text: Knight in action is fancied

indicators.note: in places the knight's title inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action
Sir is the title given to a knight

explanation.surface: A knight in battle is admired by the ladies.
explanation.definitionFit: To be desired is to be wanted or longed for, which is what fancied means.

clue.text: Master plan's beginning with a radio-controlled aircraft

indicators.note: a word's beginning is its opening letter, taken from plan's

parts.note: a drone is an unmanned aircraft flown by remote radio control

explanation.surface: The boss's plan starts with a drone.
explanation.definitionFit: A padrone is an Italian word for a master, boss or patron, especially an employer.

clue.text: Press in rapture over newspaper leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: The press is delighted by newspaper editorials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' and 'newspaper leaders' suggest journalism; a newspaper leader is an editorial, but here it means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them flat with a heated appliance.

clue.text: Caribbean island — make houses popular, it being in recession

indicators.note: houses means the brand word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a marque is a make or brand, especially of car

indicators.note: being in recession means going backwards, so the words popular and it are read in reverse order

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Caribbean island makes homes popular even when the economy is in recession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in recession' turns INIT round to TINI, which goes inside MARQUE.
explanation.definitionFit: This French overseas territory lies in the Lesser Antilles in the Caribbean Sea.

clue.text: Author feeding the last character to lion in meal, I suspect

indicators.note: in places the fed lion inside the rearranged letters of the meal and I
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are not in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: feeding the letter to the lion means pushing it into the lion's word

parts.note: Leo is the lion of the zodiac
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An author feeds the final scraps to a lion at mealtime, I suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges MEAL and I into EMILA; LEZO (Z put inside LEO by 'feeding') goes inside it, 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Emile Zola was a French novelist, writer of Germinal and the open letter J'accuse.

clue.text: A division of a company contracted to be proficient

indicators.note: contracted means the word is shortened to its usual abbreviation, dropping its middle letters

parts.note: a department is a division of a company

explanation.surface: A section of a firm hired on contract proves skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means highly skilled or expert, the same as being proficient at something.

clue.text: French leave resort at once, tanned by end of vacation

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here from vacation
to re-sort is to sort again, putting the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Returning from a French holiday resort at once, suntanned by the end of the vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is the anagram signal, read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: French leave is an idiom for absence without permission, that is, failing to turn up.

clue.text: Self-appointed authority supports breakfast club

parts.note: to back is to support, so backs means supports
to breakfast is to eat the morning meal
a driver is a golf club for long shots

explanation.surface: A self-styled leader sponsors a club that meets for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breakfast club' reads as a group; 'breakfast' is a verb, eat, and 'club' is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names a passenger who gives unwanted directions, someone who assumes authority without being asked.

clue.text: Promotion that is for everyone, cheers

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a promotion
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone, universal

explanation.surface: An advert, suitable for all audiences, raises a cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is an informal British way of saying goodbye, as is this French farewell.

clue.text: Nut, a seed that can stick on a bird

parts.note: a nut or kook is a crazy person
a burr is a seed head with hooks that sticks to fur and clothes

explanation.surface: A crazy person sticks a burr on a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kookaburra is a large Australian kingfisher known for its laughing call.

clue.text: Trade on the up in worthless goods? Most unlikely

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for worthless goods

parts.note: tat is cheap worthless stuff

indicators.note: on the up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, in reverse

parts.note: to sell is to trade goods

explanation.surface: Trading upwards in junk is the least likely way to get rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' reverses SELL to LLES in this down clue. 'Tall' means far-fetched, as in a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall can mean exaggerated or hard to believe, as in a tall tale, so the superlative is the least credible.

clue.text: Revolution dismissed in assembly

parts.note: a turn is a revolution or rotation
in cricket a batsman who is dismissed is out

explanation.surface: A revolution was dismissed by the assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT for dismissed comes from cricket, where a dismissed batsman is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnout is the gathering of people who attend an event, an assembly of attenders.

clue.text: Prison sentence for the enemy?

definitions.meaning: doing ... means serving a term in jail
the old saying holds that the passing of hours is the enemy of all

explanation.definitionFit: Serving a prison term is called doing time, and time is proverbially the enemy that ages everyone.

clue.text: Magic words in typos, here, wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly means the letters are written in the wrong order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Magic words appear in typos here because they were wrongly spelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror says this exclamation as a trick reaches its climax, so it is a magician's catchphrase.

clue.text: A weed? Get a grip! Be brave!

definitions.meaning: read literally, it means take hold of a stinging weed firmly
figuratively, it urges facing a difficulty boldly

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means tackling a problem boldly, from grasping a stinging plant firmly so it does not sting.

clue.text: Labourer being taken care of conjointly

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in a farm hand
a matter in hand is being dealt with or taken care of

explanation.surface: A labourer is being looked after with others jointly.
explanation.definitionFit: Going hand in hand means together or in close association, which is what conjointly means.

clue.text: Wangle a discount for the keeper

indicators.note: to wangle is to manipulate or fiddle, so the letters are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: Someone tries to wangle a discount from the shopkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a guardian or caretaker, someone who keeps something safe.

clue.text: Duck's first, and stew to keep going

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Duck's is taken

parts.note: a ragout is a highly seasoned stew

explanation.surface: Duck goes in first, and the stew is left to simmer on.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag something out is to prolong it, making it continue longer than needed.

clue.text: Contact guzzling too much soup

indicators.note: guzzling means one word swallows the other inside it

parts.note: to page someone is to contact them by pager or call
OTT, over the top, means too much

explanation.surface: A contact is guzzling far too much soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Pottage is an old word for a thick soup or stew, as in a mess of pottage.

clue.text: Woman ruling man

definitions.meaning: a female monarch reigning over a country
a chessman, the most powerful piece on the board

explanation.surface: A woman ruling a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A reigning female monarch has this title, and it is also a chess piece, a chessman.

clue.text: Scorer found in striker, naturally

indicators.note: found in means the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A goal scorer is found in the striker, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' suggests a footballer, but it means someone who writes musical scores: Jerome Kern, composer of Show Boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome Kern was an American composer of musicals, so he wrote scores.
